title: Testing JavaScript Apps
tagline: Write tests that catch real bugs, run fast and never cry wolf.
description: Most teams don't lack tests; they lack tests they trust. This course teaches you to write the kind that earn their place: unit tests that pin down behaviour, UI tests that act like a user, and end-to-end tests that don't flake. You use Vitest, Testing Library and Playwright, the tools most JavaScript teams run in 2026.

Everything is built around Splitwise-lite, a bill-splitting module with real money bugs waiting to happen: rounding, leftover cents, async saves and a settle-up algorithm. In the playground you write tests against working code, then prove them by catching deliberately broken versions, the same idea behind mutation testing, which you meet properly at the end.
audience: JavaScript developers who can build a small app and want tests that give them real confidence to change it.
prerequisites: Comfortable with modern JavaScript (functions, arrays, promises, async/await) and basic DOM or React.
learnItems: Choose the right mix of unit, integration and end-to-end tests
Write clear Vitest tests with edge cases and table-driven cases
Test errors, async code and collaborators without over-mocking
Test UI the way users use it, with Testing Library queries
Write Playwright tests that wait correctly and don't flake
Judge a suite with coverage, mutation testing and CI signals
